action.rationale: Fresh problem with dim=10 and a large budget of 2000 (≥ 20·dim=200); spending ~12% (~240 evals) on probes on a cheap, deterministic objective will inform structure and the right method before committing.

Probes indicate a smooth, likely single-basin landscape: P5 cosine = 1.0 (gradients reliable), P3 quadratic R² (rank) = 0.974, and short L-BFGS-B runs achieved large gains (P4 rel_gain = 0.95) with modest endpoint spread (y_spread = 0.304). Starting from the incumbent y = 4871.57, polishing with L-BFGS-B should rapidly drive down the objective to near-optimal levels.

Probes indicate a smooth, likely single-basin landscape (P5 cosine 1.0, P4 gain 0.95 with y_spread 0.304, P3 quad R² 0.97+). L-BFGS-B just delivered a large improvement (−4716 over 300 evals), is still active (exhausted=false), and recent improvements continue (stall_evals=2), so continuing it should efficiently reduce the value further.

Probes indicate a smooth single basin (P5 cosine_min=1.0; P4 rel_gain=0.9495, endpoint_y_spread=0.3038), so lbfgsb is appropriate. The active lbfgsb is still improving (best 155.382→153.937 last round), not exhausted, and stall_evals=14 ≪ 200.

Probes indicate a smooth near-single-basin landscape (P5 cosine=1.0; P3 quad R²=0.982; P4 rel_gain=0.95 with endpoint_y_spread=0.304), and the active lbfgsb has not exhausted. It is still improving (best 151.745 at eval 735), so continuing lbfgsb should gain further in the shortest time.

Probes indicate a smooth single basin (P5 cosine=1.0, P3 quad R²_rank=0.974, P4 y_spread=0.304≈single-basin), so lbfgsb remains appropriate. The active lbfgsb is not exhausted and just improved the incumbent to 150.256 with only 5 stall evals, and recent rounds show steady gains (~1–1.5 per 100 evals). Continuing should yield further decrease before convergence.

Probes indicate a smooth single basin (P5 cosine=1.0, P4 y_spread=0.304, P3 quad R²=0.982), so lbfgsb remains the fastest choice. The active lbfgsb has not exhausted and is still improving (best 150.17 → 149.28 last round; stall_evals=6). Continuing should let it converge further.

Probes indicate a smooth single basin (P5 cosine=1.0, P3 quad R² rank=0.974, P4 gain=0.95 and y_spread≈0.304), favoring gradient-based polishing. The active lbfgsb is still improving and not exhausted (stall_evals=7, exhausted=false), having just improved this round from 149.28 to 149.151. Continuing should yield small but steady gains.

LBFGSB is exhausted at the incumbent (y=149.15 at eval 1106; active.exhausted=true), so this basin is done. With 893 evals left (> 3 rounds) and probes showing smooth structure (P5 cosine=1.0, P3 R²≈0.98), the next step is to explore for potentially better basins via CMA-ES with an IPOP-style diverse restart. We will polish any new basin’s best point afterward.

Probes indicate a smooth single basin (P5 cosine=1.0, P3 quad R²=0.982, P4 gain=0.95 with y_spread=0.304), while CMA-ES ran 100 evals with 0 improvement and a poor best (1372). L-BFGS-B plateaued at 149.15 after 869 evals, so switching to BOBYQA to refine the incumbent is the best use of budget now.

Probes indicate a smooth single basin (P5 cosine=1.0, P3 quad R²=0.982, P4 gain=0.95, y_spread=0.304), and both local methods have effectively converged: lbfgsb spent 869 evals and plateaued at 149.15, while bobyqa’s last 150 evals improved only 3.8e-08 with stall_evals=260. Further budget is unlikely to improve upon 149.15, so we stop to save 643 evaluations.
